description: The Flood Risk and Flood Events Map is the Water Resources Authority of Jamaica's public web map of where the island floods. The map item and its feature service, read on 2026-09-28, hold a point layer of 3,226 recorded flood events with location, parish, watershed unit, event name, date, flood type, depth, width, area, duration, verification and source, compiled from the authority, the University of the West Indies at Mona and other government agencies. Floodplain layers give 5 to 100-year extents for six rivers from studies of 1990 to 1994, 2003 and 2011, islandwide 2 to 100-year GEOGloWS floodplains from a rapid raster model, flooded areas after Hurricane Melissa, past local flood extents and OpenStreetMap buildings, in 93 service layers. Coverage is Jamaica. Access is free as an ArcGIS feature service; the item restricts use to research purposes and names no open licence. Caveats: the event record is not exhaustive, points do not show flood extent or magnitude, some locations were estimated from media reports, and the floodplain studies are decades old. It supports flood exposure and emergency studies, such as overlaying floodplains and event hotspots on roads, water supply and buildings. Related records: the Jamaica infrastructure risk and resilience assessment and the NWC reservoir levels.
